03What It IsOVERVIEW▶

A Claude skill that builds a Fusion CAM settings dashboard for one toolpath operation (2D Offset Roughing, 2D Pocket, Adaptive, Contour, Drill, Parallel and so on). Swami uploads the operation's settings as a CSV (columns Tab,Group,Parameter,Value,Default) or as JSON with the same keys, and a Fusion Doc JSON of that operation's Autodesk documentation page, made with the fusion-doc-json skill's page.

Claude writes a notes.json with the thinking: every Fusion expression worked out for this tool (tool_diameter*.5 becomes 0.1875 in), a Setup at a Glance table, advisory review notes and a glossary. The skill's own Python builder then lays out the page on the current vibe-dashboard template: Search, one section per dialog tab, Changed from Default, Review Notes, the Full Parameter List, a Mind Map, the Glossary, References and the export verbatim. Claude adds the audio overview last. The reference build is the 2D Offset Roughing dashboard.

Why it mattersA CAM operation's dialog hides dozens of settings behind expressions and defaults. One page that shows each value as a real number for this cutter, flags what was changed, and quotes Autodesk's own description makes a toolpath easy to check before cutting.
04What It DoesOVERVIEW▶
  • Resolve ExpressionsWorks out every Fusion expression for the tool (diameter, corner radius, spindle speed, feeds), reads ; as a comma in functions, and marks settings switched off by a parent as (inactive). Values the export can't supply, such as flute count or library stepover, are flagged, never invented.
  • Setup at a GlanceA 10 to 14 row table of the key settings resolved to numbers (tool, speed and SFM, feeds, chip load, stepdown, stepover, entry, heights, stock to leave, direction, coolant), plus a Math used callout.
  • Tab SectionsOne section per dialog tab, in export order, with Parameter, Value, Resolved and Status columns. The Heights tab also gets a height stack table.
  • Doc LinesMatches each exported row to its Autodesk doc setting and shows the doc's first sentence under the name, plus the chosen option's description (for example Helix).
  • Changed from DefaultLists every setting the export marks as not default, shown as CHANGED in pink.
  • Review NotesFour to eight advisory notes, most important first: tool name versus diameter, missing values, no stock to leave on roughing, feeds versus chip load, Both Ways, leads, ramp versus plunge, colliding heights.
  • Full Parameter ListEvery row, sortable, plus a table of settings that are in the documentation but not in the export.
  • References and SourceLinks to the Autodesk doc page and related pages, and reproduces the export file verbatim.
  • Search, Mind Map, Glossary, AudioAdds vibe-dashboard's Search section, Mind Map and fitted tables, a Glossary of the CAM terms on the page, and a spoken audio overview, like every other vibe-dashboard.
  • Without DocsIf Swami says to go ahead without the Doc JSON, it builds the page without doc lines, the docs-only table and References.

08Capabilities and LimitationsSCOPE▶
  • Any OperationWorks for any CAM operation whose settings export with the five columns, as CSV or JSON.
  • Real NumbersShows each expression as a number for this cutter, with units and the formula.
  • Docs Beside ValuesPuts Autodesk's own description of each setting, and of the chosen option, next to the value.
  • Honest GapsFlags values the export doesn't carry instead of guessing, and lists documented settings the export left out.
  • RepeatableThe builder gives every operation the same layout, so dashboards for different toolpaths read alike.
  • One OperationOne dashboard per operation; it doesn't compare operations or cover a whole setup.
  • Export OnlyOnly knows what the export carries; tool-library values such as flute count, stepover or ramp angle stay unknown unless Swami supplies them.
  • Advice, Not VerificationReview notes are observations to check, not a simulation or a guarantee the toolpath is safe.
  • Name MatchingDoc matching relies on names; when the export and the doc use different wording, a setting goes unmatched and is listed as docs-only.
  • Export MethodThe skill takes the settings as CSV or JSON but doesn't say how to export them from Fusion.

11GotchasGOTCHAS▶
  • Tool Name vs DiameterA tool's name can contradict its real diameter (named 1/4 in, defined 0.375 in). The skill checks and raises it first.
  • Missing Library ValuesFlute count, tool_stepover, tool_rampAngle and similar aren't in the export; the page says so instead of inventing them.
  • SemicolonsFusion's export writes function arguments with ; (Math.min(a; b)); they are read as commas.
  • Unresolved RowsThe builder prints every expression row it can't turn into a number; each must be added to notes.resolved before publishing.
  • Repeated Group NamesIf a group name appears in two tabs, its resolved keys need the tab too (Tab|Group|Parameter).
  • Don't Hand-editEdits go into notes.json or the builder and the page is rebuilt; hand edits to the HTML are lost on the next build.
  • Glossary TermsEvery glossary term must appear in the page body; the builder warns about any it can't find, and Claude rewords them before publishing.
  • Windows DownloadsOn Windows the exported settings file and saved doc page land in C:\Users\<name>\Downloads unless you choose another folder.

TermTopicDefinitionAppears inQty
CAM operationFusion CAMOne toolpath in Fusion's Manufacture workspace, such as 2D Pocket or Adaptive, with its own settings dialog.
Settings exportInputsThe operation's settings as a CSV or JSON file with Tab, Group, Parameter, Value and Default columns.
Fusion Doc JSONInputsAutodesk's documentation page for the operation, turned into operation > tabs > sections > settings JSON.
notes.jsonBuilderClaude's notes for the page: resolved values, the glance table, review notes and optional text.
BuilderBuilderThe skill's Python script that lays out the dashboard from the settings export, doc JSON and notes, and applies vibe-dashboard's patches.
ExpressionFusion CAMA formula in a setting, such as tool_diameter*.5, that Fusion evaluates for the current tool.
Resolved valueBuilderAn exported value turned into a real number with units for this tool.
UnresolvedBuilderA row the builder couldn't turn into a number; it must be added to the notes.
InactiveFusion CAMA setting that a switched-off parent setting disables, such as Lead-In radius when Lead-In is off.
DefaultFusion CAMFusion's out-of-the-box value; the export marks each row Yes (default), No (changed) or N/A.
Doc lineBuilderThe grey first sentence of Autodesk's description shown under each parameter name.
SFMMachiningSurface feet per minute: how fast the cutting edge moves; π × diameter × rpm ÷ 12.
Chip loadMachiningMaterial removed per tooth per revolution: feed ÷ (rpm × flutes).
StepdownMachiningHow deep each pass cuts.
StepoverMachiningHow far sideways each pass moves.
Stock to leaveMachiningMaterial a roughing pass leaves for a later finishing pass.
RampMachiningEntering the material on an angle or helix instead of plunging straight down.
Both WaysMachiningCutting in both directions, mixing climb and conventional milling.
